hints: Notice what actually changes in each test, forming $\text{I}_2$ from $\text{I}^-$ is a change in oxidation state, while forming $\text{HCl}$ from $\text{Cl}^-$ is not.
Remember that $2\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 2e^-$ is oxidation by loss of electrons, so something else must gain those electrons and be reduced.
Think about the trend down Group 17 and decide which halide ion gives up its electrons more easily to the concentrated acid.
walkthrough:
**Spot acid-base versus redox**

With $\text{NaCl}$, you get steamy white fumes of $\text{HCl}$. That is just a proton transfer, the $\text{Cl}^-$ stays as $\text{Cl}^-$ in $\text{HCl}$.

$$\text{NaCl(s) + H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(l)} \rightarrow \text{NaHSO}_4\text{(s) + HCl(g)}$$

**Spot the oxidation with iodide**

With $\text{NaI}$, you get purple vapour of $\text{I}_2$. Here $\text{I}^-$ with oxidation state -1 has become $\text{I}_2$ with oxidation state 0, so it has been oxidised.

$$2\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 2e^-$$

**Identify the roles and the trend**

If iodide is oxidised, concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ must be reduced, so the acid is acting as an oxidising agent. It is strong enough to oxidise $\text{I}^-$ but not $\text{Cl}^-$, which tells us iodide ions are more easily oxidised than chloride ions.

options.A: It is correct that sulfuric acid acts as an oxidising agent here, but the trend is backwards. If chloride were more easily oxidised, you would see $\text{Cl}_2$ and not $\text{I}_2$, which is the opposite of the observation.
options.B: Correct and reassuring. Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is reduced (to $\text{SO}_2$, S and $\text{H}_2\text{S}$) while it oxidises $\text{I}^-$ to $\text{I}_2$. $\text{Cl}^-$ is held more tightly and is harder to oxidise, so it only does the acid-base reaction to give $\text{HCl}$.
options.C: Sulfuric acid is not the reducing agent here, it is the species that gains electrons and is reduced. Also, $\text{Cl}^-$ to $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{I}^-$ to $\text{I}_2$ involve oxidation (loss of electrons), not reduction.
options.D: This reverses the roles. The halide ions are the ones being oxidised (electron donors), not reduced. Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is the oxidising agent that accepts those electrons.
